en.heading: 28 January: Julian Felipe Day is non-working only in Cavite City
en.origin: Julian Felipe Day honours the composer of the music of the Philippine national anthem. Born on 28 January, Julian Felipe is closely associated with Cavite City and the history of the country's national symbols. Republic Act No. 7805, which became law on 1 September 1994 without the President's signature, designated 28 January every year as a special non-working public holiday specifically in Cavite City. The statute recognizes his role in creating the national anthem's music, but its local jurisdiction is explicit. The Cavite City non-working rule must not be repeated as if it granted a day off throughout the Philippines.

en.heading: 4 October: Philippine Kindness to Animals Day began in 1958
en.origin: Kindness to Animals Day invites Philippine communities to treat animals with compassion and to reject cruelty. Its calendar is aligned with the wider international animal-welfare observance on 4 October. Proclamation No. 537, signed by President Carlos P. Garcia on 30 September 1958, established 4 October every year as Kindness to Animals Day in the Philippines, asking schools and civic bodies to participate. Proclamation No. 1112, signed on 27 July 2006, reiterated the same annual date and broad civic participation. This later proclamation confirms the observance but does not make 2006 the year of its first national designation.

en.heading: 19 September: the Order of Gabriela Silang in the Philippine Honors Code
en.origin: The Order of Gabriela Silang is one of the official honors listed by the Philippine state. It carries the name of Gabriela Silang, a figure of resistance against Spanish colonial rule in the eighteenth century. Executive Order No. 236, dated 19 September 2003, established the Honors Code and placed the Order of Gabriela Silang in the third tier of civilian honors, separating its protocol status from other named orders. The Code says that the order may be awarded to spouses of Filipino or foreign heads of state or government. Its purpose differs from the Order of Lakandula, which recognizes political and civic merit, even though both appear in the same 2003 code.

en.heading: 19 September: the Order of Lakandula recognizes political and civic service
en.origin: The Order of Lakandula is a major Philippine state honor named for a historical leader associated with prudent service to his people. Its categories recognize contributions to civic life, political responsibility, peace and public welfare. Executive Order No. 236 of 19 September 2003 introduced the Honors Code ranking and placed the Order of Lakandula in the senior second tier alongside the Order of Sikatuna and the Philippine Legion of Honor. The Code lists ranks from Grand Collar to Member and eligibility for Filipinos or foreigners who have demonstrated outstanding civic or political merit. This is not the Order of Gabriela Silang for spouses of heads of state, despite the identical code date.

en.purpose: Clarify the political-civic criteria and why two orders share a legal code without becoming duplicate honors.
facts: The Order of Lakandula is a major Philippine state honor named for a historical leader associated with prudent service to his people. Its categories recognize contributions to civic life, political responsibility, peace and public welfare.

Executive Order No. 236 of 19 September 2003 introduced the Honors Code ranking and placed the Order of Lakandula in the senior second tier alongside the Order of Sikatuna and the Philippine Legion of Honor.

The Code lists ranks from Grand Collar to Member and eligibility for Filipinos or foreigners who have demonstrated outstanding civic or political merit. This is not the Order of Gabriela Silang for spouses of heads of state, despite the identical code date.

it.heading: 19 settembre: l'Ordine di Lakandula premia il merito politico e civico

L'Ordine esecutivo n. 236 del 19 settembre 2003 ha introdotto il Codice delle onorificenze e collocato Lakandula al secondo livello con Sikatuna e la Legione d'onore filippina. Il Codice elenca gradi dal Gran Collare al Membro e destinatari filippini o stranieri distinti per meriti politici e civici. Non è l'Ordine di Gabriela Silang per i coniugi dei capi di Stato, nonostante la stessa data.

de.heading: 19. September: Lakandula-Orden für politischen und bürgerschaftlichen Dienst
de.origin: Der Lakandula-Orden ist eine bedeutende Staatsehrung, benannt nach einem historischen Anführer. Er würdigt bürgerschaftliches Engagement, politische Verantwortung, Frieden und Gemeinwohl. Executive Order Nr. 236 vom 19. September 2003 schuf die Ehrenordnung und platzierte Lakandula in der zweiten Stufe neben Sikatuna und der Philippinischen Ehrenlegion. Der Kodex definiert Stufen vom Großcollier bis zum Mitglied für philippinische und ausländische Personen mit politischem oder zivilem Verdienst. Er ist nicht der Gabriela-Silang-Orden für Ehepartner von Staatschefs.
